text:
Winnipeg has the look of a team stuck between gears. The Jets are 6-8-3, 2-7-1 over their last 10, but at 47% of the expected goals they are closer to average than the record. The bigger gap is at the other end: 45 goals scored against 52.1 expected, a seven-goal shortfall that is costing them games.

The top line is doing its job. Mark Scheifele, Kyle Connor and Cole Perfetti have played 161 minutes together, creating 3.53 expected goals per 60 and outscoring opponents 9-6. Dylan Samberg and Neal Pionk, the top pair, are just above even on chances in 218 minutes. The problem is the penalty kill, allowing 0.9 expected goals a game, and depth that doesn't add much scoring behind the top unit.

There has been some life this week. Captain Adam Lowry set up the overtime winner after Tuesday's rally, which Ken Wiebe of the Winnipeg Free Press wrote about, and the Jets followed with a lopsided win over Vancouver. Connor Hellebuyck addressed fans in a notebook item at Daily Faceoff; as a team, Winnipeg's goals against (60) are right in line with its chances (59.5 expected).

Our simulations project 81 points and give them a 13% playoff chance. That is low for a team with these chances. If the shooting simply comes back to normal, the Jets could make the next month look very different, starting with Tampa.
headline: The Jets are waiting on their goals
